Chat vs Project vs Cowork

Three ways to work with AI at School Tech. Once you're past the basics, knowing which one to reach for saves real time. Here's what each is, when to use it, and where each one bites.
For Staff - Intermediate
Quick frame
  • Plain chat - a blank conversation with no School Tech setup. Fast, personal, forgets everything when you close it.
  • Project - a chat pre-loaded with School Tech context and reference files. This is what you use for real work day to day.
  • Cowork - a desktop app where Claude can actually do things - work with files on your computer, run code, and run jobs on a schedule. Admins and power users only.
Not sure which you're in? If it already knows School Tech, you're in a Project. If it can open files on your computer, that's Cowork. Otherwise it's a plain chat.

Plain chat

What it is: a fresh conversation with no STA setup. It knows nothing about us unless you paste it in, and it starts blank every time you open a new one.

Reach for it when: you want a quick reword, a definition, a one-off rewrite, or a personal question that has nothing to do with STA data.

STA examples: "Reword this sentence to sound friendlier." "What does SAML mean in plain English?" "Draft a quick thank-you note."

Watch out: it forgets everything when you close it, and it has zero School Tech context.
Projects

What it is: a chat that's pre-loaded with School Tech instructions and reference files (a built-in knowledge base). It already knows our products, customers, processes, and tone, so you skip the explaining and just ask.

Where you find it: a Project is a Claude.ai Project, and you open it from the Chat tab (top-left). Every staff tool - AI Advisor, STA Support Chat, Salesforce Cohort - is a Project you reach from the Chat tab. This is the surface staff use day to day. (Not to be confused with Cowork, which lives on its own separate Cowork tab - see below.)

Our live Projects: AI Advisor (all staff), STA Support Chat (support team), Salesforce Cohort (any Salesforce user, mostly our SF admins).

Reach for it when: you're doing real STA work - troubleshooting, customer drafts, Salesforce guidance - or anything a teammate should be able to use too, since Projects are shareable.

Good to know: a Project keeps its setup files loaded every time, but it still won't recall yesterday's conversation unless that info lives in the project.

Gotcha: connectors like Gmail and Drive only work in a PRIVATE project. The moment a project is shared with the team, connectors switch off.
Cowork

What it is: the desktop app where Claude can take real action - read and write files on your computer, run code, run jobs on a schedule, and split big tasks into sub-tasks. It's the "do things for me" surface, not just "answer me."

Where you find it: Cowork uses its own separate Cowork tab - not the Chat tab where Projects live. We deliberately say "Project" for the Chat-tab tools and "Cowork" for the Cowork-tab workspace; they are not the same thing. The Cowork tab is for admins and power users.

Who has it at STA: admins and power users only.

Worth it when: multi-file work, a recurring or scheduled output (like a weekly digest), or a long multi-step job that would overwhelm a single chat. For anything that's just one question, use a Project instead - Cowork uses more of our usage allowance.

Needs your computer awake: scheduled jobs skip if the machine is asleep or the app is closed.

Data caution - important: Cowork has no audit log and stores its data on your local computer. Anthropic's own guidance is not to use it for regulated work. For School Tech that means never run student records, HR or employee PII, or any restricted data through Cowork. The data rule from the Getting Started guide applies double here.
Which one do I use?
  • Just need an answer, a definition, or a quick rewrite? → Plain chat
  • Doing real STA work, or something a teammate should use too? → a Project
  • Need it to touch files on your computer, or run on a schedule? → Cowork (and you're an admin or power user)
Common gotchas
  • Plain chat forgets everything the moment you close it.
  • Shared Projects lose connector access (Gmail, Drive) - keep a project private if it needs them.
  • Cowork only runs while your computer is on and awake.
  • Cowork uses more usage than a Project - don't reach for it for one-off questions.
  • Cowork is never for student, HR, or restricted data - there's no audit trail.
